```{r}
#| include: false
library(master)
library(fiber)
set.seed(7)
```

# Scope

This document is the reference for the per-bundle pyramidal-tract (PyT)
module of `master`. It first summarises the *understood anatomy* of the human
pyramidal tract — what the module treats as ground truth and the sources it
follows — then derives the *mathematical model* implemented in `R/pyramid.R`.
The code itself is the executable form of the model; this text states the
assumptions it encodes and the anatomical conventions it fixes.

**Locked decisions.** The modelling decisions below are fixed and form the
contract the module must satisfy. Each is derived in the section it links to.

1. **Somatotopic completeness.** One bundle per body-part parcel
   (`leg`, `trunk`, `arm`, `hand`, `face`); each hemisphere carries the
   complete contralateral homunculus (@sec-table).
2. **Ground-truth mean pathway.** The parcel mean pathway `c_k(s)` is the
   deterministic object a tractography algorithm should recover; the FDA
   perturbation is zero-mean, so the bundle sample mean stays exactly on it
   (@sec-pathways, @sec-perturbation).
3. **No split, no fusion.** The decussation is a per-streamline sign
   flip on `q`; streamlines never split and branches never fuse
   (@sec-decussation).
4. **Landing side by the flip alone.** From the crus down, `q` is
   single-signed and ascending `leg → face`; the flip `φ(s)` alone decides
   whether a fibre lands contralateral (`crossed`) or ipsilateral
   (`uncrossed`) (@sec-table, @sec-decussation).
5. **Corticobulbar face.** The `face` parcel stops at the pons, its flip
   completes exactly at the pons, and it takes no posterior detour — the
   bilateral termination of the corticobulbar projection (@sec-decussation).
6. **Anatomically scaled spread.** Each axon's displacement from its parcel
   centreline is rescaled by the local section half-width `γ(s)`, so bundle
   width tracks the cross-section (@sec-perturbation).

# Anatomy of the pyramidal tract {#sec-anatomy}

## Macroscopic course

The *pyramidal tract* is the principal motor pathway of the human central
nervous system: the collection of axons that originate from the primary motor
cortex (Brodmann area 4, the precentral gyrus and the anterior bank of the
central sulcus), descend through the corona radiata, the posterior limb of the
internal capsule, the crus cerebri of the midbrain, the basis pontis, and the
medullary pyramids, and then — for the majority of fibres — cross the midline
at the pyramidal decussation to continue in the contralateral lateral
corticospinal tract of the spinal cord [@lassek1948neurons; @lassek1954pyramidal; @nieuwenhuys2008human].

The tract is composed of two anatomically and functionally distinct
subsystems, distinguished by their termination:

- **Corticospinal fibres** continue past the medulla into the spinal cord. In
  the cord they run, in overwhelming majority, in the *lateral* corticospinal
  tract (contralateral to their cortex of origin); a small *ventral*
  (anterior) corticospinal component descends ipsilaterally. The majority of
  corticospinal fibres cross at the decussation, the remainder descending
  ipsilaterally [@lassek1948neurons; @lassek1954pyramidal].
- **Corticobulbar fibres** terminate in the brainstem, on the motor nuclei of
  the cranial nerves. The majority of the corticobulbar projection to the
  lower cranial-nerve motor nuclei is *bilateral* (each hemisphere projects to
  both sides), with the notable exception of the lower-face subnucleus of the
  facial nucleus, which receives an overwhelmingly contralateral projection
  [@kuypers1958corticobulbar].

The two subsystems leave the cortex intermingled in the same fan and can only
be separated by their terminal targets, not by their initial course. The
mapping of this split onto parcels — `face` as the corticobulbar
representative ending at the pons, limb/trunk parcels as corticospinal fibres
running to the cord — is a modelling choice described in @sec-stations.

## Somatotopic organisation

Within the precentral gyrus the body is represented as an orderly strip — the
*motor homunculus* — with the lower limb on the medial wall of the
hemisphere, the trunk, arm and hand across the convexity, and the face on the
inferior lateral precentral gyrus [@penfield1950cerebral]. This medial-to-
lateral order along the precentral strip constrains the model's cortical
*u*-order (see @sec-table). The same somatotopic sequence is preserved as a
*sheet* through the corona radiata and funnels into the internal capsule,
where it rotates so that, at the posterior limb, the leg fibres lie
posteriorly and the face anteriorly in the antero-posterior direction
[@nieuwenhuys2008human].

The somatotopic arrangement continues into the brainstem and cord: at the
pyramidal decussation and in the lateral corticospinal tract the fibres from
the leg lie most medially and the face most laterally, so the order along the
strip is preserved but re-rotated onto the medial-lateral axis of the cord
[@lassek1954pyramidal; @nieuwenhuys2008human]. The model transcribes this
order into the *single-signed, medial-to-lateral* `q`-rows of the somatotopic
table from the crus downward (see @sec-table).

## The decussation and its geometry

The majority of corticospinal fibres cross the midline at the pyramidal
decussation at the junction of medulla and spinal cord, sweeping posterolaterally
and interleaving with the fibres that remain uncrossed before descending in the
contralateral lateral corticospinal tract [@lassek1954pyramidal;
@nathan1955long]. The crossing is oblique rather than a single midline plane;
crossed and uncrossed fibres interdigitate in the decussation volume before
sorting into their respective lateral tracts.

How the model implements the crossing as a per-streamline event — and why
that preserves the single-path and no-fusion properties — is described in
@sec-decussation.

## What the model treats as ground truth

@tbl-anatomy summarises the anatomical statements the module treats as
non-negotiable, with the sources.

::: {#tbl-anatomy}

| Statement | Source |
|---|---|
| PyT originates in the primary motor cortex and descends to the cord | @lassek1954pyramidal; @nieuwenhuys2008human |
| Corticospinal fibres mostly cross at the decussation | @lassek1954pyramidal; @nathan1955long |
| Corticobulbar fibres terminate in the brainstem, mostly bilaterally | @kuypers1958corticobulbar |
| Cortical motor somatotopy: leg medial → face lateral | @penfield1950cerebral |
| Cord somatotopy: leg medial, face lateral in the lateral corticospinal tract | @lassek1954pyramidal; @nieuwenhuys2008human |
| Crossed and uncrossed fibres interlace at the decussation | @nathan1955long |

Anatomical statements treated as ground truth by the module.
:::

# Mathematical model {#sec-model}

## Coordinate frame

The model works in a right-handed anatomical coordinate system. $X$ is the
medial–lateral axis with $X = 0$ at the midline (positive $X$ = right
hemibody); $Y$ the anterior–posterior axis (positive anterior); $Z$ the
inferior–superior axis with the motor cortex at $Z = 0$ and the cord at
$Z = -\texttt{tract\_length}$.

A **macro-axis** $A(s)$ — the mean pathway of the whole tract as a function of
a normalised abscissa $s \in [0, 1]$ — is swept as a straight vertical drop
along $Z$ with a small anterior bow:

$$A(s) = \big(0,\ \beta \sin(\pi s),\ -\ell\, s\big), \qquad \ell = \texttt{tract\_length} = 70\text{ mm}, \qquad \beta = \texttt{bow} = 1.5\text{ mm}.$$ {#eq-macroaxis}

(The bow approximates the gentle anterior convexity of the tract's course through
the corona radiata.) Per hemisphere the macro-axis is offset laterally by
$\pm\texttt{midline\_offset}$.

A smooth **moving frame** $(e_u, e_v, T)$ is defined along the macro-axis:
$T$ is the unit tangent, $u$ a smooth cross-section axis, and
$v = u \times T$, so the frame stays orthonormal and the cross-section never
shears. The twist of the frame along the tract is controlled by a map
$\psi(s)$, with control points $\psi_{st}$ given at the anatomical stations
(@sec-stations) and interpolated by the C1 smoothstep

$$\psi(s) = \texttt{smoothstep\_interp}(s, s_{st}, \psi_{st}).$$

Internally the model uses the simple frame $S_u = (\pm 1, 0, 0)$ (toward the
midline for each hemisphere), $S_v = S_u \times T$, rotated by $\psi$:

$$e_u = \cos\psi\, S_u + \sin\psi\, S_v, \qquad e_v = -\sin\psi\, S_u + \cos\psi\, S_v.$$ {#eq-frame}

## Anatomical stations {#sec-stations}

All control tables are pinned to a common grid of nine **anatomical stations**
along the tract, from motor cortex to spinal cord, given as a fraction of the
total arc length by `pyt_stations()`:

| Station | fraction | depth (mm) | Station | fraction | depth (mm) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cortex | 0.00 | 0 | pons | 0.60 | 42 |
| corona | 0.10 | 7 | pyramid | 0.72 | 50 |
| centrum | 0.20 | 14 | dec | 0.82 | 57 |
| ic | 0.35 | 24 | cord | 1.00 | 70 |
| crus | 0.50 | 35 | | | |

The stations delimit the anatomical events of @sec-anatomy: the fan at the
cortex/centrum, the rotation at the internal capsule (`ic`), the re-rotation
at the crus–midbrain (`crus`), the pons (where the corticobulbar `face` parcel
terminates), the medullary pyramid, the decussation (`dec`, where the crossed
branches flip), and the cord. Every continuous field of the model — twist,
widths, and the per-parcel `q`/`r` positions — is given as control points at
these stations and interpolated between them by the C1 smoothstep, so the
whole model is specified by the table and the stations it is pinned to.

## The somatotopic table {#sec-table}

Each body-part parcel $k \in \{\texttt{leg}, \texttt{trunk}, \texttt{arm},
\texttt{hand}, \texttt{face}\}$ is placed in the cross-section of the tract by
two coordinates, `q` (along $e_u$) and `r` (along $e_v$), given as control
points at the stations of @sec-stations and interpolated to any $s$ by the
same C1 smoothstep. The section widths $W_u(s)$, $W_v(s)$ scale the two axes.
The default table is produced by `pyt_defaults()`.

The table encodes three anatomical facts, all verifiable against the sources
of @sec-anatomy:

1. **Cortical fan.** At the cortex the parcels tile the $u$-axis in the order
   $\texttt{leg} < \texttt{trunk} < \texttt{arm} < \texttt{hand} <
   \texttt{face}$ ([@penfield1950cerebral]; values in `q_st["cortex", ]`), spread
   over the full width $W_u(\text{cortex}) = 40$ mm.
2. **Rotation at the internal capsule.** At the `ic` station the twist
   $\psi = \pi/2$ rotates the sheet so the same order projects onto the
   anterior–posterior axis of the capsule, and at the crus–midbrain the frame
   re-aligns to the medial–lateral axis of the brainstem
   ([@nieuwenhuys2008human]; `q_st["ic", ]` + `twist`).
3. **Single-signed medial–lateral order from the crus down.** From the `crus`
   station onward the rows of `q_st` are single-signed and strictly ascending
   (leg most medial, face most lateral), matching the cord order described by
   @lassek1954pyramidal and @nieuwenhuys2008human. This single-signed
   convention is deliberate: it makes the decussation flip (below) the *only*
   mechanism that decides the landing side of a fibre, so a crossed fibre lands
   contralateral and an uncrossed fibre ipsilateral by construction
   (@sec-decussation).

The per-parcel **terminal station** separates the corticospinal parcels (which
run to the `cord`) from the corticobulbar `face` parcel (which stops at the
`pons`, @sec-anatomy [@kuypers1958corticobulbar]).

## Parcel mean pathways {#sec-pathways}

For a parcel $k$ the interpolated fields `q_k(s)`, `r_k(s)` and the widths
$W_u(s)$, $W_v(s)$ define its **mean pathway** — the deterministic centreline of
that parcel's bundle:

$$c_k(s) = A(s) + W_u(s)\, q_k(s)\, e_u(s) + W_v(s)\, r_k(s)\, e_v(s).$$ {#eq-parcel}

The three fields are all C1-smooth (smoothstep interpolation), so each
`c_k` is a smooth curve. The parcel mean pathway is the *ground truth* of the
module: it is the deterministic object that a tractography algorithm should
recover, and the FDA perturbation below is constructed to keep the sample mean
of the bundle exactly on it.

## The decussation as a per-streamline sign flip {#sec-decussation}

A fibre is assigned to a **branch**: `uncrossed` ($\varphi = +1$) or
`crossed` ($\varphi = -1$), the latter with probability
`cross_percent = 0.85`. For the crossed branch the `q`-field of the parcel is
multiplied by a smooth C1 taper $\phi(s)$ that goes from $+1$ to $-1$ over a
short window of width `cross_span` centred on the `dec` station (for the
limb/trunk parcels):

$$\phi(s) = \cos\big(\pi\, \texttt{smoothstep}(t)\big), \qquad
t = \frac{s - s_{\text{lo}}}{s_{\text{hi}} - s_{\text{lo}}}.$$ {#eq-phi}

The crossed fibre therefore sweeps smoothly from its ipsilateral medial
position, across the midline, to the mirror-position on the contralateral
side. Because `q` carries the single-signed medial–lateral convention, the
flip alone decides the landing side and the two branches of a parcel end on
opposite sides of the cord — the interdigitating X of the decussation
([@nathan1955long]).

Two refinements complete the picture:

- **Posterior detour.** For the limb/trunk parcels a smooth bump
  `cross_detour * sin(pi * smoothstep(t))` is added to the `r` coordinate in
  the flip window, pushing the crossed fibres posterolaterally as they cross —
  the oblique, not transverse, character of the real decussation.
- **Centroid shift.** A `center_gap` lateral offset is added to the crossed
  branch so its streams visibly interlace with the uncrossed copy rather than
  overlapping it.
- **The face exception.** The corticobulbar (face) parcel flips over the
  window `[pons − span, pons]` — completing exactly at the pons — and takes no
  posterior detour, modelling the bilateral termination of @sec-anatomy: both
  branches of the face parcel end at the pons, on opposite sides
  ([@kuypers1958corticobulbar]).

The flip is applied **per streamline** (to `q_k` before the axon perturbation,
equivalently to every sample of the parcel's centreline), never to the bundle
as a whole, so no streamline ever splits and the two branches never fuse, by
construction.

## Axon populations: the FDA perturbation {#sec-perturbation}

Each parcel's mean pathway `c_k(s)` is populated with `n_axons = 30` axons per
branch using the same FDA machinery as the rest of `master`
([@ramsay2005fda]; `create_axons()`): the *i*-th axon of the parcel is

$$x_{k,i}(s) = c_k(s) + \varepsilon_{k,i}(s),$$ {#eq-axon}

where each of the three coordinates of the perturbation
$\varepsilon_{k,i}$ is a linear combination of `n_basis = 8` B-splines over the
centreline abscissa, with zero-mean Gaussian coefficients having exponential
autocorrelation

$$\mathrm{Cov}\big[\varepsilon^{(c)}(s), \varepsilon^{(c)}(s')\big] = \sigma^2 \exp\!\Big(-\frac{|i-j|}{\texttt{autocorrelation}}\Big), \qquad \sigma^2 = \texttt{variance} = 0.02.$$ {#eq-cov}

Two properties follow. First, the perturbation is **zero-mean** on each axon's
coordinate field and hence on the bundle sample mean, so the parcel mean stays
exactly on the ground-truth `c_k(s)` regardless of `variance` (the central
validation property of the module). Second, the autocorrelation makes
neighbouring coefficients coherent, so streamlines are smooth, parallel-ish
axons rather than independent random walks.

**Spread scaling.** The coefficient variance alone (0.02) would yield a bundle
only ~0.13 mm RMS wide, far below the ~1 mm parcel tiling of the tract, so the
module additionally rescales each axon's displacement from its parcel
centreline by the local mean section half-width

$$\gamma(s) = \frac{W_u(s) + W_v(s)}{4},$$ {#eq-gamma}

i.e. the implemented perturbation is $\gamma(s)\,\varepsilon_{k,i}(s)$. The
resulting within-branch RMS deviation tracks the anatomy of the cross-section:
~1.6 mm at the cortex, ~0.3 mm at the internal capsule, ~0.6 mm at the pons,
~0.3 mm at the cord. Bundles read as narrow but contiguous clouds instead of
hairline strokes, and the zero-mean property is preserved (the scaling applies
to the zero-mean displacement field).

# Verification {#sec-verification}

The model's geometry is verified numerically in `inst/tinytest/test_pyramid.R`
(150 assertions) and, for the reader, by the following figure: the left and
right pyramidal tracts rendered as their mean pathways (one streamline per
parcel branch), with the decussation interval shaded and the two hemispheres
mirrored across the midline.

```{r}
#| label: fig-pyt
#| fig-cap: "Left and right pyramidal tracts (mean pathways, by parcel)."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 6

L <- simulate_pyramidal_tract(hemisphere = "left", seed = 7)
R <- simulate_pyramidal_tract(hemisphere = "right", seed = 7)

one <- function(bs, i, br) {
  b <- bs@bundles[[i]]
  idx <- which(b@streamline_data$branch == br)[1]
  b@streamlines[[idx]]@points
}
parcels <- c("leg", "trunk", "arm", "hand", "face")
cols <- c("#ff9441", "#e3622e", "#b84324", "#7d2a18", "#4a1f2e")

plot.new()
plot.window(xlim = c(-25, 25), ylim = c(-75, 8))
axis(1); axis(2)
title(xlab = "X (mm, medial-lateral)", ylab = "Z (mm, cortex = 0)")
for (k in seq_along(parcels)) {
  for (h in list(L, R)) {
    for (br in c("uncrossed", "crossed")) {
      p <- one(h, k, br)
      lines(p[, "X"], p[, "Z"], col = cols[k], lwd = if (br == "crossed") 1.2 else 0.7)
    }
  }
}
abline(h = -70 * 0.82, lty = 3, col = "grey50")   # decussation station
abline(h = -70 * 0.60, lty = 2, col = "grey70")   # pons station
legend("bottomright", legend = parcels, col = cols, lwd = 2, bty = "n")
```

The figure uses one mean streamline per parcel branch, so the deterministic
geometry (fan, funnel, rotatory twist, decussation mirror, interdigitating
crossings) is visible without the sampling noise of the full 60-axon bundles.
For the interactive three-dimensional rendering of the full bundles, run

```r
fiber::bind_bundle_sets(
  simulate_pyramidal_tract(hemisphere = "left", seed = 7),
  simulate_pyramidal_tract(hemisphere = "right", seed = 7)
) |> rtists::plot3d(color = "parcel", backend = "plotly")
```

# Summary

The module encodes, per hemisphere, one bundle per body-part parcel:
`leg`, `trunk`, `arm`, `hand`, `face`. Each parcel has a deterministic mean
pathway (fan at the cortex, funnel at the IC, re-rotation at the crus–midbrain,
single-signed medial–lateral order from the crus down), is populated by
zero-mean FDA axons scaled to the local cross-section, and is split into an
uncrossed and a crossed branch by a per-streamline C1 sign flip at the
decussation. The `face` parcel is the corticobulbar representative: it ends at
the pons, bilaterally. The anatomical assumptions, sources and the mathematical
definitions above make the module reproducible as documented in this file.
